rows.selection_reason: With no completed experiments, the main uncertainty is the performance floor and whether a simple RNA-only model is already competitive. config_001 tests a minimal RNA-only PCA single-profile baseline, avoiding confounds from multiprofile aggregation, image encoding, and fusion. This is the best first experiment because it establishes a clear reference point for later comparisons of RNA encoders, profile settings, image-only models, and multimodal fusion.

The only completed experiment is a single-profile RNA-only PCA baseline, so there is still no evidence about whether the image modality is informative. Testing image-only single-profile ResNet50 gives a clean unimodal image baseline, isolating the image representation effect without adding aggregation or fusion complexity. This is the best next experiment because it reduces uncertainty about a major design choice—whether image features are worth using—before spending budget on multimodal fusion or more complex profile settings.

RNA-only PCA singleprofile (config_001) is much stronger than image-only ResNet (config_010) in both accuracy and F1, making RNA the current promising direction. The key uncertainty is whether multiple profiles add useful information beyond the single-profile baseline. config_002 keeps the same RNA encoder and uses avgpool, the simplest aggregation for multiprofile, so it tests the profile/aggregation effect with minimal added complexity. This is an efficient exploitation of the best current evidence and will clarify whether to invest further in multiprofile, transformer aggregation, or fusion.

RNA-only multiprofile PCA with avgpool is the strongest result so far, clearly better than singleprofile PCA and far above weak image-only ResNet. The key unresolved factor in this promising branch is aggregation: avgpool versus transformer. Testing config_003 keeps the RNA encoder and profile setting fixed, isolates the aggregation effect, and indicates whether transformer aggregation is worth pursuing before adding more complex multimodal or fusion choices.

The strongest evidence so far is that PCA-based RNA with multiprofile avgpool is the best configuration (0.5907 accuracy, 0.5727 F1), outperforming singleprofile PCA and transformer aggregation, while the only image-only test is weak. The key uncertainty is whether a learned RNA encoder can improve on PCA under this promising profile/aggregation setting. config_005 tests this by changing only the RNA encoder to scvi_n200 while keeping multiprofile avgpool, isolating the representation effect. This is an efficient next experiment because it has high expected performance, avoids confounding changes from image modality or fusion, and will clarify whether stronger RNA representations are worth pursuing before investing in multimodal configurations.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only models dominate image-only, and the strongest result is config_005 (scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool) with validation accuracy 0.650 and F1 0.628, improving over PCA multiprofile avgpool. The key uncertainty is whether this gain is specific to scvi_n200 or whether another pretrained RNA encoder, scgpt, can match or exceed it under the same profile and aggregation. config_008 changes only the RNA encoder while keeping multiprofile and avgpool fixed, directly isolating the representation choice. This is the best next experiment because it exploits the strongest RNA-only direction, has plausible high immediate performance, and will clarify which RNA encoder should be used before testing more complex multimodal configurations.

The strongest completed configuration is RNA multiprofile scvi_n200 with avgpool, with validation accuracy 0.650 and F1 0.628, and avgpool also outperformed transformer for PCA. Image-only ResNet50 singleprofile is weak, so whether image features can add value is uncertain. This experiment tests whether adding image features to the best RNA configuration via simple concat fusion improves validation accuracy/F1 while keeping the RNA encoder, profile setting, and aggregation fixed. It is the best next use of budget because it exploits the strongest known direction and directly clarifies the key multimodal fusion question before moving to more complex image encoders or fusion variants.

The strongest RNA-only result is multiprofile scvi_n200 with avgpool (config_005, acc 0.650, F1 0.628). The closest multimodal test using the same RNA encoder, profile, and aggregation but concat fusion (config_030) is slightly worse (acc 0.632, F1 0.607), leaving uncertainty about whether the image modality can help under a different fusion rule. config_031 changes only fusion from concat to weighted, isolating the effect of fusion while keeping the otherwise promising design fixed. This is a high-value exploitation step: if it improves, it shows weighted fusion may make multimodal profiling competitive; if not, it supports focusing on the RNA-only configuration.

RNA multiprofile scvi avgpool is strong (0.650 acc, 0.628 F1), and multimodal scvi/resnet avgpool weighted is the current best (0.678 acc, 0.646 F1), but only modestly above RNA-only, while image-only single resnet is very weak (0.208 acc). The key uncertainty is whether the image modality can contribute at all under the multiprofile/avgpool setting used in the best multimodal runs. config_011 tests image-only with the same resnet encoder, multiprofile setting, and avgpool aggregation, isolating the image stream’s contribution before investing further in multimodal or stronger image encoders. This is a high-value, budget-efficient experiment because it clarifies whether future effort should focus on image representation/fusion or primarily on RNA-side design choices.

The strongest evidence is config_031 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) with 0.678 accuracy and 0.646 F1, which beats RNA-only scvi avgpool and also shows weighted fusion improving over concat. The key remaining uncertainty in this promising region is aggregation: avgpool is strong, but transformer aggregation is untested for scvi with weighted fusion. config_033 changes only aggregation from avgpool to transformer, isolating that effect while exploiting the best known encoder and fusion setup. This is a high-value next experiment because it may improve on the current best or clarify whether transformer aggregation adds value before exploring new image encoders.
